problem: Existing embodied AI benchmarks are mostly indoor or built on fictional/simplified cities (MetaUrban, GRUtopia, AerialVLN) or on street-view/satellite imagery (Touchdown, V-IRL, CityNav) with only discrete movement and few tasks, so open real-city embodied intelligence is under-evaluated.
motivation: Embodied agents need to operate in open outdoor urban environments to approach AGI and have real-world value, but no platform offers a high-fidelity real-city 3D simulator with continuous control, dynamic traffic and systematic tasks. The authors build one from a real Beijing district and use it to probe current multimodal LLMs.
key_idea: Build a UE5/AirSim-based, high-fidelity 3D replica of a real Beijing district with dynamic pedestrians and vehicles, drone/vehicle interfaces, and a five-task benchmark (scene understanding, QA, dialogue, VLN, task planning) with 87.1k human-refined cases.
insight: The benchmark discriminates model capability: GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 clearly outperform small open models (Fuyu-8B, Qwen-VL) on QA, dialogue and scene understanding, and all models degrade on long vs short VLN routes (e.g. GPT-4o SR 76.92 short vs 20.00 long). Counting and position questions remain hard even for large models. Human refinement of LLM-generated ground truth is essential since raw VLM outputs contain wrong counts, existence and positions.
method: 3D city environment: 2.8km x 2.4km Beijing business district in Unreal Engine 5.3, ~200 buildings modeled by hand in Blender from street-view, 100 streets (~50 km), 6k+ urban elements, plus a nearby residential area with interiors
Dynamic traffic: vehicle and pedestrian flows simulated using the Mirage Simulation System with historical real traffic data

Agent interface: AirSim-based first-person observations (RGB, depth, segmentation, IMU, GPS, LiDAR, state) and continuous control for drones (target position/velocity/orientation, camera) and vehicles (steering, throttle, brake, gear)
SDK and online platform: Python client SDK plus HTTP proxy server over AirSim (sync/async), online platform supporting up to 8 agents via keyboard, web GUI or code editor with live video
Benchmark tasks: five tasks (12.2k scene understanding, 50.4k QA on distance/position/counting, 12.6k dialogue, 1.3k VLN, 10.6k task planning) using 8 directional views plus top-down image

Data labeling: GPT-4o/VLM auto-generated prompts and answers followed by manual refinement (fixing counting/existence/position errors, removing negative, unplanned or redundant responses); VLN start/goal and trajectories human-annotated
Evaluation: BLEU/ROUGE/METEOR/CIDEr/Sentence-BERT for text tasks; SR, SPL, NE for VLN, on Fuyu-8B, Qwen-VL, Claude 3 (Haiku), GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-4o

setting.backbone: Fuyu-8B, Qwen-VL, Claude 3 Haiku, GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-4o (all frozen, prompted)
setting.training_data: none (zero-shot evaluation of pretrained MLLMs; benchmark data 87.1k cases)
setting.observation: first-person RGB from 8 directions plus top-down view (depth, segmentation, LiDAR, GPS, IMU available in simulator)
setting.action_space: continuous drone control (position/velocity/orientation) and vehicle control (steering/throttle/brake); VLN in the paper's evaluation controls a drone

numbers.extra: 1.3k-case VLN set; NE in meters; success radius not stated

numbers_note: Benchmark paper; baselines are evaluated LLMs, so only LLM results are recorded. Only some metrics listed for text tasks (QA, planning omitted per-type detail). Test split naming is assumed since the paper doesn't specify splits.
results: GPT-4 Turbo dominates QA (e.g. Distance BLEU-1 76.63) and dialogue, while Claude 3 leads scene understanding and task planning. On VLN, GPT-4o and Claude 3 reach the best mean SR 34.90 / SPL 34.25 with GPT-4o having the lowest NE (90.11 m); all models perform far worse on long routes.
limitations: Only prompted MLLMs are evaluated; no trained navigation baselines and VLN set is small (1.3k cases) with high NE (~90-160 m)
Ground truth for most tasks is LLM-generated then refined, which may introduce bias; text-overlap metrics poorly capture correctness
Sim2Real validation is only planned, and only one Beijing district is modeled
